name: Kerberos Error Reference (Every Common Error + Fix)
command: # match your Kerberos error below and apply the fix
description: Quick reference for the Kerberos errors you hit running impacket / certipy / Rubeus / evil-winrm from Linux against AD, and how to fix each one. Saves time chasing phantom failures during a chain.
source: HTB Fluffy engagement; common AD-from-Linux errors
notes:
=== KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW (Clock skew too great) ===
  Cause: host clock differs from the DC by > 5 min.
  Fix:   sudo ntpdate <dc_ip>   (or wrap with faketime) -> ad-faketime-kerberos

=== KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED ===
  Meaning: the account requires pre-auth (NOT AS-REP roastable). Normal - move on.

=== KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN ===
  Cause: username/realm wrong, or SPN/host does not exist.
  Fix:   check the case and realm (UPPERCASE realm), verify the account/SPN exists,
         use the FQDN not the IP for -spn/-target.

=== KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN ===
  Cause: the target SPN does not exist (getST/S4U).
  Fix:   confirm the SPN (setspn -q / Get-DomainUser -SPN); use cifs/<fqdn> exactly.

=== KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED ===
  Cause: wrong password/hash, or wrong etype.
  Fix:   verify creds; for PtH use -hashes :<nthash>; try AES if RC4 is disabled.

=== KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED ===
  Cause: wrong service key / wrong SPN / wrong target host (ticket for another service).
  Fix:   request the ticket for the exact SPN of the service you are hitting; use FQDN.

=== KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP ===
  Cause: requested encryption type not supported (often RC4 disabled).
  Fix:   use AES (-aesKey) or let the tool negotiate; regenerate the ticket.

=== KDC_ERR_WRONG_REALM / referrals ===
  Fix:   set the correct realm; for cross-domain, target the right DC (-dc-ip of that domain).

=== 'KRB_AP_ERR_TKT_EXPIRED' ===
  Fix:   ticket expired - request a fresh TGT (getTGT.py) and retry.

=== NAME RESOLUTION (not a Kerberos error but breaks it) ===
  Add the DC/host to /etc/hosts (IP  dc01.domain.local domain.local) so FQDNs resolve;
  Kerberos is name-sensitive - use FQDNs, not IPs, for SPNs.

=== GENERAL CHECKLIST ===
  1. Clock in sync?  2. Realm UPPERCASE?  3. FQDN (not IP) for SPNs?  4. /etc/hosts set?
  5. KRB5CCNAME exported?  6. Right etype (AES vs RC4)?

examples.label: Add DC to /etc/hosts for name resolution
